subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 10
source.subtopic: Addition and subtraction up to 6 (weeks 1-2), 7 (weeks 3-4), 8 (weeks 5-6), 9 (weeks 7-8) and 10 (weeks 9-10) using +, -, =, □

show.line: Four plus two equals six. Six take away two equals four. Plus adds, minus takes away!

rounds.prompt: Three red cars and three blue cars. How many altogether?
rounds.praise: Six! Three plus three equals six.

rounds.prompt: Five plus one. Tap the answer.
Six minus four. How many are left? Say the number.
Which number sentence shows the picture? Two plus four.
rounds.praise: Yes! Two plus four equals six.

rounds.prompt: Six minus three. Tap the answer.
Four plus the box equals six. What goes in the box?
rounds.praise: Two! Four plus two equals six.

hints: Plus means count on. Minus means count back.
Use counters or your fingers. Count them all.

beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Minus means take away. Six minus one equals five.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's count back together. Six, and one less is five!

parent_line: Can add and subtract to 6 and read plus, minus and equals.
